programme: TP53 and TP73 (p53-family paralogs) converge with MEF2D on the same downstream effectors — CDKN1A and GADD45A — to run a stress-triggered cell-cycle-arrest/apoptosis checkpoint; MEF2D itself sits on this checkpoint as a target of GSK3beta phosphorylation that tips it toward driving apoptotic transcription rather than survival transcription.
role_in_a: In neurons this checkpoint is aberrantly engaged rather than protective: GSK3beta-phosphorylated MEF2D is diverted from its normal pro-survival programme toward apoptotic gene expression (PMID 19801631), reproduced in an APP/PS1 model where a compound that corrects this rescues memory (PMID 35718493); TP53 is separately implicated as a modulatable node in AD pathology (PMID 42353021). TP73's contribution is unresolved — the one retrieved AD study explicitly found no association in mouse models or human cohorts (PMID 23414597).
role_in_b: In mammary epithelium the same checkpoint is the tumor's obstacle to overcome: TP53 mutation status is a major clinical prognostic and predictive marker (poor survival, altered treatment response — PMIDs 42607633, 42174712, 42446626), TP73/TP73-AS1 is studied as a biomarker and therapeutic re-activation target including in triple-negative disease (PMIDs 40332793, 40849803, 40011499), and MEF2D acts directly as a tumor suppressor whose loss permits growth (PMID 38791246).
shared_axis: Both tissues run the same p53-family/MEF2D → CDKN1A/GADD45A checkpoint, but the pathology sits on opposite sides of it: AD involves inappropriate over-activation driving neuronal apoptosis, while breast cancer involves its disablement (via TP53 mutation or MEF2D loss) permitting escape from apoptosis. This mirrors the well-known epidemiological inverse association between cancer and Alzheimer's disease, for which divergent p53-pathway engagement is a standard mechanistic candidate — though that specific literature is not among the papers retrieved here.
reasoning: TP53 (234/312) and MEF2D (165/312) are each independently and mechanistically placed in both diseases by the retrieved papers, and their target sets genuinely converge on CDKN1A/GADD45A, so the module is nameable without recourse to outside knowledge. But TP73's AD evidence is a negative finding rather than support, and no retrieved paper connects AD and breast cancer through this axis jointly — the connection is inference from each disease's separate literature, not a documented fact about the pair.
support: PMID 42353021 — TP53 implicated in modulating Alzheimer's disease pathology; PMID 42607633 — TP53 mutation predicts poor breast-cancer-specific survival; PMID 42446626 — TP53 autoantibodies as diagnostic biomarker in mammary tumours; PMID 42174712 — TP53 mutation linked to CDK4/6-inhibitor treatment duration in breast cancer; PMID 23414597 — TP73 shows no association with Alzheimer's disease in mouse models or human cohorts (negative finding); PMID 40332793 — TP73-AS1 as biomarker/therapeutic target in cancer including breast; PMID 40849803 — TP73-targeted nintedanib strategy in triple-negative breast cancer; PMID 40011499 — TP73 methylation pattern differs in triple-negative breast cancer; PMID 35718493 — MEF2D-linked pathway rescued in an AD mouse model; PMID 19801631 — GSK3beta phosphorylation of MEF2D drives neuronal apoptosis; PMID 38791246 — MEF2D functions as a tumor suppressor in breast cancer.
how_to_falsify: Compare CDKN1A/GADD45A induction downstream of TP53/TP73/MEF2D in AD-affected hippocampal neurons (e.g. single-nucleus RNA-seq of AD vs control brain) against TP53-mutant vs TP53-wildtype breast tumors: if the AD neurons do not show concordant checkpoint-target induction, or if TP53-mutant tumors escape apoptosis through mechanisms that bypass CDKN1A/GADD45A entirely, the shared-checkpoint account fails. A well-powered AD GWAS/expression replication that confirms TP73's null result would also require dropping TP73 from the module.
caveats: 312 patient-group comparisons across 6 independent cohort pairs is a reasonably broad base, but brain and breast are anatomically and clinically unconnected tissues, so any shared axis rests on convergent pathway biology, not shared physiology. TP73's role is the weakest link — its only AD evidence is a non-association finding. Several other concordant factors (GATA3, NR5A2, PAX2, ZNF165, HOXC9, VSX1, PATZ1, NFYB, BMAL2) were not included because they show breast-cancer-specific or, for BMAL2, an entirely separate circadian-clock story (PER1/PER2/BHLHE40/41 targets) with its own direct AD and breast-cancer support — a distinct candidate programme not folded in here since only one coherent module was named. The single-view factors (ZHX3, ZFP64, HOXB13, POU4F1, HTATIP2, MYRF, WWTR1, SOX1) and tissue-generic factors (ZEB1, SOX10, HDAC7, STAT4, TAL1, EGR4, NR3C1, RFX5, NOTCH1) play no role in this account, consistent with their exclusion.
